title: Body Repair: Health, Safety and General Precautions
introduction: A body repair restores more than the shape you can see. I read it in layers: protection for the person doing the work, the strength of the repaired structure and the restraint system's ability to do its job afterward. A tidy panel gap tells only part of that story. Use these precautions alongside the repair-specific workshop instructions; this overview does not teach welding, restraint-system access or collision repair as standalone procedures.

edits.text: WARNING: Whenever handling chemicals, consult the Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) and wear the protective equipment it directs. Depending on the chemical, this may include respirators and chemically resistant gloves; these examples are not exhaustive. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Choose protection from the information for the actual chemical being used, rather than assuming the same equipment suits every body-repair product.

edits.text: WARNING: Always wear protective equipment when sanding or grinding, including eye protection with side shields and a dust mask. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: The required protection addresses both airborne dust and material thrown toward the eyes.

edits.text: WARNING: Do not perform body side sectioning repairs in the areas of door hinge or striker anchoring points. Welding within 50 mm (1.96 in) of a door hinge or striker location may compromise structural integrity during a collision. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious injury to vehicle occupant(s).
edits.why: A hinge or striker anchorage has a structural role beyond making the door fit. Treat these locations as restrictions when planning the repair.

edits.text: WARNING: Welding emits invisible ultraviolet and infrared radiation that can injure unprotected eyes and skin. Always use protection such as a welder's helmet fitted with dark-colored filter lenses of the correct density. Because electric welding produces intense radiation, filter plate lenses of the deepest shade that still provides adequate visibility are recommended. People working in the weld area are strongly advised to wear flash safety goggles. Also wear protective clothing. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Protection is needed for exposed skin as well as eyes, and the recommendation for people in the weld area extends beyond the person holding the welding equipment.

edits.text: WARNING: Every collision repair must include inspection and correction of all safety belt components. Inspect them as prescribed in Safety Belt Inspection and Repair After a Collision, in Section 501-20A General Procedures of this manual. Failure to follow this instruction may cause incorrect safety belt system operation and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: The required inspection covers the complete safety belt system. Use the named procedure for its inspection method and repair decisions; this warning alone does not supply them.

edits.text: WARNING: After a crash, inspect the Restraints Control Module (RCM) and impact sensor mounting areas for damage or deformation. Inspect related components for cracks, damage and loose fasteners as well. If a mounting area is damaged, restore it to the original production configuration. After that area is repaired, replace the original RCM or impact sensor at that location with a new component, whether or not the airbags deployed. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: The RCM monitors restraint inputs and commands deployment when required. The inspection therefore includes its mounting environment. Restoring a damaged mounting area comes before the mandatory replacement of the component at that location; lack of airbag deployment does not cancel that requirement.

edits.text: WARNING: Carry out collision damage repairs according to the instructions in this workshop manual. Replacement components must be new, genuine Ford Motor Company parts. Ford does not authorize recycled, salvaged, aftermarket or reconditioned parts, including body parts, wheels or safety restraint components.
edits.why: I treat the prescribed repair method and replacement parts as a matched set. Both requirements serve the repaired vehicle's structural integrity and crash safety.

edits.text: Departing from this manual's instructions—including using alternate repair methods or substitute components—risks compromising crash safety. Failure to follow these instructions may adversely affect structural integrity and crash safety performance, which could result in serious personal injury to vehicle occupants in a crash.
edits.why: I look beyond how neatly the panels line up: the repaired structure also has a job to do in a crash. Appearance alone cannot confirm that the required repair method and components have been used.
